from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_str = "The Problem: The Noisy Cosmic Message"
        lecture_strs = [
            "Meet Byte, sending data from Mars to Earth.",
            "Space radiation can flip bits during transmission.",
            "Errors turn clear messages into garbled noise."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lecture_strs)

        # Assets - Replaced missing ImageMobjects with placeholder VMobjects
        mars = Circle(color=RED, fill_opacity=1) # [Asset: mars.png]
        earth = Circle(color=BLUE, fill_opacity=1) # [Asset: earth.png]
        byte_robot = Square(color=GREY, fill_opacity=1) # [Asset: robot_byte.png]
        radiation = Triangle(color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=1) # [Asset: radiation_bolt.png]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.place_in_area(mars, "A1", "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(earth, "E5", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(byte_robot, "B1", scale_factor=0.4)
        
        # We start with the 4-bit message
        bits = VGroup(*[Text(b, font_size=36, color=YELLOW) for b in "1011"])
        bits.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(bits, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(mars), FadeIn(earth), FadeIn(byte_robot))
        self.play(Write(bits))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(RED)
        
        self.place_at_grid(radiation, "C3", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(radiation))
        
        # Travel towards Earth, but get hit at C3
        self.play(bits.animate.move_to(self.grid["C3"]), run_time=1.5)
        
        # Bit flip animation
        flash = Flash(self.grid["C3"], color=RED, num_lines=8)
        
        # Third bit is index 2
        old_bit = bits[2]
        new_bit = Text("0", font_size=36, color=RED)
        # Manually align new_bit to old_bit's position within the moving group
        new_bit.move_to(old_bit.get_center())
        
        self.play(flash)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(old_bit, shift=UP),
            FadeIn(new_bit, shift=UP)
        )
        # Update the group to include the new bit for future animations
        bits.remove(old_bit)
        bits.insert(2, new_bit)
        
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(ORANGE)
        
        # Finish journey to Earth
        self.play(bits.animate.move_to(self.grid["E5"]), run_time=1.5)
        
        q_mark = Text("?", font_size=48, color=ORANGE)
        self.place_at_grid(q_mark, "D5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(q_mark))
        self.play(Indicate(earth, color=ORANGE))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Prerequisite: The Simple Parity Bit"
        lines = [
            "A parity bit helps detect single errors.",
            "We add one bit to make '1's even.",
            "If the count is odd, we know something broke."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Display '101'
        data1 = Text("1 0 1", font_size=36)

        # Highlight two 1s

        highlight2 = data1[-1]
        
        self.play(Write(data1))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(
            highlight1.animate.set_color(BLUE_C),
            highlight2.animate.set_color(BLUE_C)
        )
        
        # Add '0' parity bit
        parity1 = Text("0", font_size=36, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(parity1, "B4")
        
        arrow1 = Arrow(start=data1.get_right(), end=parity1.get_left(), buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(arrow1), FadeIn(parity1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )

        data2 = Text("1 1 1", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(data2, "D2")
        
        # Highlight three 1s
        self.play(Write(data2))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(data2.animate.set_color(BLUE_C))
        
        # Add '1' parity bit
        parity2 = Text("1", font_size=36, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(parity2, "D4")
        
        arrow2 = Arrow(start=data2.get_right(), end=parity2.get_left(), buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(arrow2), FadeIn(parity2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Label the extra bit 'Parity' in #FFFF00

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Limitation: Detection vs. Correction", [
            "Parity tells us an error exists.",
            "But it cannot show which bit is wrong.",
            "To fix data, we need more clever guards."
        ])

        # Colors
        SENT_COLOR = BLUE_C
        RCVD_COLOR = RED_C
        TEXT_COLOR = WHITE

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Parity tells us an error exists.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        sent_label = Text("SENT:", font_size=24, color=SENT_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(sent_label, "A1")
        
        sent_bits = VGroup(*[Text(b, font_size=36, color=SENT_COLOR) for b in "1010"]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(sent_bits, "A2", "A5")
        
        rcvd_label = Text("RCVD:", font_size=24, color=RCVD_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(rcvd_label, "C1")
        
        rcvd_bits = VGroup(*[Text(b, font_size=36, color=RCVD_COLOR) for b in "1000"]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(rcvd_bits, "C2", "C5")
        
        self.play(Write(sent_label), Write(sent_bits))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(Write(rcvd_label), Write(rcvd_bits))
        
        # Parity check logic
        parity_note = Text("Sum = 1 (Odd) -> ERROR!", font_size=20, color=RED)
        self.place_in_area(parity_note, "D1", "D6")
        self.play(FadeIn(parity_note))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # But it cannot show which bit is wrong.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Siren effect
        siren = Circle(radius=0.5, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.3).set_stroke(RED, 5)
        self.place_in_area(siren, "C2", "C5")
        
        def siren_updater(m, dt):
            m.set_stroke(width=10 * np.sin(self.time * 10) + 10)
            m.set_fill(opacity=0.3 * np.abs(np.sin(self.time * 10)))

        siren.add_updater(siren_updater)
        self.add(siren)
        
        question_text = Text("Which bit is the liar?", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(question_text, "E1", "E6")
        
        # Highlight bits
        highlights = VGroup(*[SurroundingRectangle(b, color=YELLOW, buff=0.1) for b in rcvd_bits])
        
        self.play(Write(question_text))
        self.play(Create(highlights))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # To fix data, we need more clever guards.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        guards_text = Text("Need 'Guards' in specific spots...", font_size=22, color=BLUE_A)
        self.place_in_area(guards_text, "F1", "F6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(guards_text))
        self.wait(2)
        
        siren.remove_updater(siren_updater)
        self.play(FadeOut(siren), FadeOut(highlights), FadeOut(question_text), FadeOut(guards_text), FadeOut(parity_note))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Fetch data from storyboard
        title_text = "The Hamming Logic: Overlapping Venn Diagrams"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Richard Hamming used overlapping sets for control.",
            "We place data bits within multiple circles.",
            "Each parity bit monitors a specific circle.",
            "One bit change affects multiple parity checks.",
            "This overlap creates a unique error signature."
        ]
        
        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors from storyboard
        COLOR_RED = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_GREEN = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_BLUE = "#0000FF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw 3 overlapping circles: Red #FF0000, Green #00FF00, Blue #0000FF.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        circle_r = Circle(radius=1.8, color=COLOR_RED, stroke_width=4).set_fill(COLOR_RED, opacity=0.1)
        circle_g = Circle(radius=1.8, color=COLOR_GREEN, stroke_width=4).set_fill(COLOR_GREEN, opacity=0.1)
        circle_b = Circle(radius=1.8, color=COLOR_BLUE, stroke_width=4).set_fill(COLOR_BLUE, opacity=0.1)

        # Position circles to overlap on the right side grid
        self.place_in_area(circle_r, 'A3', 'C4') # Top
        self.place_in_area(circle_g, 'C2', 'E3') # Bottom-Left
        self.place_in_area(circle_b, 'C4', 'E5') # Bottom-Right

        self.play(Create(circle_r), Create(circle_g), Create(circle_b), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Place data bits d1, d2, d3, d4 in the circle intersections.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)

        d4 = Text("d4", font_size=24) # Intersection of all three
        self.place_in_area(d4, 'C3', 'D4')
        
        d1 = Text("d1", font_size=24) # Red & Green
        self.place_in_area(d1, 'B2', 'C3')
        
        d2 = Text("d2", font_size=24) # Red & Blue
        self.place_in_area(d2, 'B4', 'C5')
        
        d3 = Text("d3", font_size=24) # Green & Blue
        self.place_in_area(d3, 'D3', 'E4')

        data_bits = VGroup(d1, d2, d3, d4)
        self.play(Write(data_bits))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Place parity bits p1, p2, p3 in the outer petals.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)

        p1 = Text("p1", font_size=24, color=COLOR_RED) # Red only
        self.place_in_area(p1, 'A3', 'B4')
        
        p2 = Text("p2", font_size=24, color=COLOR_GREEN) # Green only
        self.place_in_area(p2, 'D1', 'E2')
        
        p3 = Text("p3", font_size=24, color=COLOR_BLUE) # Blue only
        self.place_in_area(p3, 'D5', 'E6')

        parity_bits = VGroup(p1, p2, p3)
        self.play(Write(parity_bits))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Highlight the Red circle and the 4 bits it monitors (p1, d1, d2, d4).
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)

        self.play(
            circle_r.animate.set_stroke(width=10, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR).set_fill(opacity=0.3),
            Indicate(p1), Indicate(d1), Indicate(d2), Indicate(d4)
        )
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(
            circle_r.animate.set_stroke(width=4, color=COLOR_RED).set_fill(opacity=0.1)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Highlight the Green circle and its own set of 4 bits (p2, d1, d3, d4).
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)

        self.play(
            circle_g.animate.set_stroke(width=10, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR).set_fill(opacity=0.3),
            Indicate(p2), Indicate(d1), Indicate(d3), Indicate(d4)
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Return to base state
        self.play(
            circle_g.animate.set_stroke(width=4, color=COLOR_GREEN).set_fill(opacity=0.1),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mapping the Positions (The Binary Address)", [
            "Parity bits live at positions 1, 2, and 4.",
            "Data bits fill the remaining available slots.",
            "Each position is a sum of unique powers.",
            "Position seven is monitored by bits 1, 2, and 4.",
            "Binary addresses tell us exactly where bits live."
        ])
        
        # Colors
        TOWER_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        CARGO_COLOR = "#00FFFF"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(TOWER_COLOR)
        
        # Create 7 slots with labels
        slots_vgroup = VGroup()
        for i in range(7):
            s = Square(side_length=0.6, color=WHITE)
            l = Text(str(i+1), font_size=16, color=WHITE).next_to(s, DOWN, buff=0.1)
            slots_vgroup.add(VGroup(s, l))
        
        slots_vgroup.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15)
        self.place_in_area(slots_vgroup, "C1", "C6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Highlight Parity Slots (1, 2, 4)
        parity_indices = [0, 1, 3] # 1, 2, 4
        for idx in parity_indices:
            slots_vgroup[idx][0].set_stroke(TOWER_COLOR, width=6)
            
        tower_label = Text("Control Towers", font_size=22, color=TOWER_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(tower_label, "B1", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(Create(slots_vgroup))
        self.play(Write(tower_label))

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_str = "The Magic Trick: Locating and Fixing"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Let's find the liar by checking all circles.",
            "If circles one and two fail, add them.",
            "One plus two equals three: the error's location!",
            "Simply flip bit three to fix the data.",
            "Error correction achieved without a re-send."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        C_NEUTRAL = WHITE
        C_FAIL = RED_A
        C_PASS = GREEN_A
        C_HIGHLIGHT = YELLOW

        # Bits representation
        # Bit values (Hamming 7,4): 1 1 0 1 1 0 0 (with an error at 3)
        bits_values = ["1", "1", "0", "1", "1", "0", "0"] 
        bit_boxes = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.7, color=C_NEUTRAL) for _ in range(7)])
        bit_labels = VGroup(*[Text(val, font_size=24) for val in bits_values])
        index_labels = VGroup(*[Text(str(i+1), font_size=16, color=GRAY) for i in range(7)])
        
        # Bits group creation
        bits_group = VGroup()
        for b, l, idx in zip(bit_boxes, bit_labels, index_labels):
            l.move_to(b.get_center())
            idx.next_to(b, DOWN, buff=0.1)
            bits_group.add(VGroup(b, l, idx))
        
        # Position bits across row D area
        self.place_in_area(bits_group, "D1", "D6", scale_factor=0.9)

        # Parity Status Indicators
        p1_indicator = VGroup(Circle(radius=0.4, color=C_NEUTRAL), Text("P1", font_size=20))
        p2_indicator = VGroup(Circle(radius=0.4, color=C_NEUTRAL), Text("P2", font_size=20))
        p4_indicator = VGroup(Circle(radius=0.4, color=C_NEUTRAL), Text("P4", font_size=20))
        
        for p in [p1_indicator, p2_indicator, p4_indicator]:
            p[1].move_to(p[0].get_center())

        self.place_at_grid(p1_indicator, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(p2_indicator, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(p4_indicator, "B4")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Let's find the liar by checking all circles.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(C_HIGHLIGHT)
        self.play(Create(bits_group))
        self.play(Create(p1_indicator), Create(p2_indicator), Create(p4_indicator))
        
        # Initial fail state for parity checks
        self.play(
            p1_indicator[0].animate.set_color(C_FAIL),
            p2_indicator[0].animate.set_color(C_FAIL),
            p4_indicator[0].animate.set_color(C_PASS),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # If circles one and two fail, add them.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(C_NEUTRAL)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(C_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        calc_text = Text("Failed: 1 + 2 = ?", font_size=28, color=C_HIGHLIGHT)
        self.place_in_area(calc_text, "A2", "A5")
        
        self.play(Write(calc_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # One plus two equals three: the error's location!
        self.lecture[1].set_color(C_NEUTRAL)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(C_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        calc_result = Text("Failed: 1 + 2 = 3", font_size=28, color=C_HIGHLIGHT)
        self.place_in_area(calc_result, "A2", "A5")
        
        self.play(Transform(calc_text, calc_result))
        
        # Highlight bit 3 (Index 2)
        self.play(
            bit_boxes[2].animate.set_color(C_FAIL),
            ScaleInPlace(bit_boxes[2], 1.2),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Simply flip bit three to fix the data.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(C_NEUTRAL)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(C_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Flip the visual value
        new_bit_label = Text("1", font_size=24, color=C_PASS).move_to(bit_boxes[2].get_center())
        
        self.play(
            Transform(bit_labels[2], new_bit_label),
            bit_boxes[2].animate.set_color(C_PASS).scale(1/1.2),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Error correction achieved without a re-send.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(C_NEUTRAL)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(C_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        success_msg = Text("Error Corrected!", font_size=32, color=C_PASS)
        checkmark = Tex(r"\checkmark", color=C_PASS, font_size=40)
        success_group = VGroup(success_msg, checkmark).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_in_area(success_group, "F2", "F5")
        
        self.play(
            p1_indicator[0].animate.set_color(C_PASS),
            p2_indicator[0].animate.set_color(C_PASS),
            FadeOut(calc_text),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(success_group))
        self.wait(2)

        # Final state cleanup
        self.lecture[4].set_color(C_NEUTRAL)

class Section7Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Real-World Application & Summary"
        lines = [
            "Hamming codes protect modern server memory.",
            "They prevent system crashes from cosmic rays.",
            "Self-healing data keeps our digital world reliable."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create RAM Stick
        pcb = Rectangle(width=4, height=1.5, color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.2)
        chips = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(width=0.6, height=0.8, color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.8)
            for _ in range(4)
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2).move_to(pcb.get_center())
        
        pins = VGroup(*[
            Line(pcb.get_bottom() + LEFT*1.8 + RIGHT*i*0.1, pcb.get_bottom() + LEFT*1.8 + RIGHT*i*0.1 + DOWN*0.15, color="#00FFFF")
            for i in range(37)
        ])
        
        ram_label = Text("ECC RAM", font_size=20, color="#00FFFF")
        ram_label.next_to(pcb, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        ram_stick = VGroup(pcb, chips, pins, ram_label)
        self.place_in_area(ram_stick, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(ram_stick))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Cosmic Ray
        ray = Line(start=self.grid["A6"], end=chips[1].get_center(), color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        ray.add_tip(tip_length=0.15)
        
        # Bit within a chip
        bit_1 = Text("1", font_size=24, color=GREEN).move_to(chips[1].get_center())
        bit_0 = Text("0", font_size=24, color=RED).move_to(chips[1].get_center())
        
        self.add(bit_1)
        self.play(Create(ray), run_time=1)
        
        # Bit flip (Error)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(bit_1, bit_0), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(ray))
        
        # Error indicator
        error_box = SurroundingRectangle(bit_0, color=RED, buff=0.05)
        self.play(Create(error_box))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Correction (Hamming magic)
        bit_1_new = Text("1", font_size=24, color=GREEN).move_to(chips[1].get_center())
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(bit_0, bit_1_new),
            error_box.animate.set_color(GREEN),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(FadeOut(error_box))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        summary_text = Text("Hamming Code: The Auto-Correct of Hardware", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(summary_text, "F3", scale_factor=0.9)
        # Shift slightly to be centered across 3-5
        summary_text.move_to((self.grid["F2"] + self.grid["F5"])/2)
        
        self.play(Write(summary_text))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Hamming Codes: The Art of Self-Healing Data
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate Computer Science students or tech-savvy high schoolers

sections.title: The Problem: The Noisy Cosmic Message
sections.content: Introduction to the concept of data corruption during transmission. Use a character-driven scenario to establish the 'Why'.
sections.example: A robot named 'Byte' is sending a secret 4-bit code '1011' from Mars to Earth. Because of cosmic radiation (noise), one bit flips from 1 to 0. Earth receives '1001'. How does Earth know it's wrong, and how does it fix it without asking Byte to resend?

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Simple Parity Bit
sections.content: Explain the foundation of error detection: the Parity Bit. Use the concept of 'Even Parity' where we add a bit to make the total number of 1s even.
sections.example: Data is '101'. There are two 1s (even), so we add a '0' as the parity bit -> '1010'. If '111' is sent, we add a '1' -> '1111'. Visual: A 'Safety Guard' bit standing at the end of a data line holding a tally counter.

sections.title: The Limitation: Detection vs. Correction
sections.content: Demonstrate that simple parity can tell us 'something is wrong' but not 'where the error is'. This creates the need for Hamming's method.
sections.example: Visual: A siren goes off on Earth because the parity doesn't match, but the technician says, 'I know there's a lie, but I don't know which bit is lying!' This is why we need more 'guards' in specific positions.

sections.title: The Hamming Logic: Overlapping Venn Diagrams
sections.content: Introduce Richard Hamming’s 7-4 Code using a visual Venn Diagram. Explain that bits are placed so they are covered by multiple overlapping parity circles.
sections.example: Visual: Three large overlapping circles (Red, Green, Blue). Data bits (d1, d2, d3, d4) sit in the intersections. Parity bits (p1, p2, p3) sit in the outer 'petals'. Each parity bit is responsible for the bits inside its specific circle.

sections.title: Mapping the Positions (The Binary Address)
sections.content: Explain why parity bits are placed at positions that are powers of 2 (1, 2, 4, 8...). This allows the binary address of the error to be calculated.
sections.example: Visual: 7 slots in a row. Slot 1, 2, and 4 are 'Control Towers' (Parity). Slots 3, 5, 6, and 7 are 'Cargo' (Data). Each Cargo bit is monitored by the Towers that add up to its position (e.g., Slot 7 is monitored by Towers 1, 2, and 4 because 1+2+4=7).

sections.title: The Magic Trick: Locating and Fixing
sections.content: Step-by-step walk-through of error correction. If multiple parity checks fail, the sum of their positions points directly to the flipped bit.
sections.example: If Parity Circle 1 and Parity Circle 2 report an error, but Parity Circle 4 is fine, we add the failed positions: 1 + 2 = 3. Bit number 3 is the liar! Visual: An animation of bit 3 flipping from a '0' back to a '1' automatically.

sections.title: Real-World Application & Summary
sections.content: Conclusion on where this is used today and the efficiency of the code.
sections.example: ECC RAM in servers and high-end workstations uses this to prevent 'Blue Screens of Death' caused by cosmic rays flipping bits in memory. Hamming codes are the 'auto-correct' of the hardware world.
